Use this sheet with [the exercise](exercise-student.html). Predict before reading the results, then explain in words. These figures use exact updating or supplied fits, with no new Stan inference.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(here)
source(here("R/functions.R"))
source(here("R/course_data.R"))
source(here("R/course_utils.R"))
source(here("R/course_visuals.R"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,fig.width=8,fig.height=4.5)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=14))
```

## The core comparison: low and high density

```{r core-results}
fit <- course_fit("day2_ndd")
draws <- fit$draws
ndd <- make_ndd_data()
plot_cndd(draws,ndd)
plot_cndd_comparison(draws)
probabilities <- cndd_probabilities(draws)
knitr::kable(probabilities |> group_by(density) |>
  summarise(median=median(p),lower=quantile(p,.025),upper=quantile(p,.975)),digits=3)
```

Density -1 is one SD below the mean, and +1 is one SD above. The fit, prior and
draws stay fixed. The probability and its interval describe uncertainty about
survival at the specified density. They do not fix a future survivor count.

## Prior scale illustration

```{r normal-scale}
plot_normal_prior_scale()
```

This Normal-response illustration follows `main.qmd`. A slope prior depends on
the units of x and y. CNDD instead has logit-scale coefficients, so the same
numerical prior SD has a different interpretation. This illustration is not a second fit.

## Instructor demonstrations

```{r demonstrations}
knitr::kable(course_diagnostics(fit),digits=2)
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(draws,pars=c("alpha","beta"))
plot_cndd_predictions(cndd_predictions(draws,n=20,seed=20261022))
replicates <- cndd_replicates(draws,ndd,seed=20261023)
plot_cndd_check(replicates,ndd)
plot_cndd_spread_check(replicates,ndd)
```

The count prediction fixes both new groups at 20 seedlings. The model check instead
retains each original quadrat's density and seedling count. It compares the observed
pattern and spread with model-generated data. These are simulated teaching data,
so compatible checks do not establish a real ecological mechanism.
